## Problem

Pinning uv (bug 56b7-b21a-c8ab-4afc) removed the VERSION-RESOLUTION manifest fetch, but CI still makes one network call to `raw.githubusercontent.com` per job, so the `##[error]fetch failed` failure mode that killed run 33214025855 is still reachable.

Verified on run 33230196661 (change 2367 patchset 1), five jobs sampled, all identical:

    Found version for uv in /home/runner/work/rebar/rebar/pyproject.toml: 0.12.7
    Fetching manifest data from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/versions/main/v1/uv.ndjson ...
    Successfully installed uv version 0.12.7

The version came from the local pin — no `Could not determine uv version` line — and the manifest was fetched anyway.

## Root cause

`setup-uv` has a SECOND, independent manifest consumer. `setupUv` (`src/setup-uv.ts`) calls `tryGetFromToolCache`; on a miss it calls `downloadVersion`, whose first statement is:

    const artifact = await getArtifact(version, arch, platform, manifestUrl);   // src/download/download-version.ts:42

The manifest supplies the download URL and sha256, so it is fetched unconditionally regardless of how the version was resolved. A GitHub-hosted runner starts each job with an empty uv tool cache, so the miss is guaranteed. This is unchanged in v10.0.1, the newest release. A committed local manifest does not help: `fetchManifestResponse` uses Node `fetch()`, which rejects `file:` URLs, and `manifest-file` is documented as a URL.

## Candidate approaches (choose ONE during planning; none is pre-selected here)

- Restore the uv binary into the runner tool cache with `actions/cache` keyed on the pinned version, so `tryGetFromToolCache` hits and `downloadVersion` never runs. Trades a raw.githubusercontent.com dependency for a GitHub-cache-service dependency, which is a different and better-instrumented failure domain — but it is still a network dependency, so state that honestly rather than claiming zero.
- Install uv without the action (direct download from `releases.astral.sh` at the pinned version with a committed sha256, mirroring the `acli` precedent in `docs/jira-sync-setup.md`). Removes the manifest entirely; costs the action's caching and PATH wiring, which would have to be reimplemented at 25 call sites or in one composite action.
- Upstream a change to `astral-sh/setup-uv` that skips `getArtifact` when the version is exact and the checksum is already in `KNOWN_CHECKSUMS`, then bump the pin.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A real CI log for the change contains the liveness anchor `Successfully installed uv version <pinned>` AND zero occurrences of `Fetching manifest data`; both greps recorded verbatim on this ticket. The anchor is asserted FIRST — a zero-match grep alone is also produced by an empty log or a skipped step, which is how an empty `gh run view --job=N --log` scored a clean vacuous pass during 56b7's verification.
- [x] The installed uv version in that same log still equals the pin in `pyproject.toml`, so the fix does not silently change which uv runs.
- [x] Whatever residual network dependency the chosen approach retains is named explicitly in the change description; the change does not claim 'no network dependency' unless the log shows zero external fetches in the install path.
